ashwin: here's a concrete Loki query for deeper inspection: ``{job="api"} |= "POST /v1/generate" | json | __error__ = "504" | line_format "{timestamp} {upstream_host} {request_id} {latency_ms}"`` — early look: 3x more 504s on cluster-eu-1 vs us-west. Also KV-cache-miss ratio for these requests is elevated: run METRIC query: ``sum(rate(kvcache_misses_total{cluster="eu-1",route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (worker) / sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total{cluster="eu-1",route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (worker)`` — shows miss/hit spike ~0.9 on affected workers.
andrew-oncall: I can repro locally against eu-edge with curl: ``curl -XPOST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"rwd-1.2","prompt":"hi"}' -v`` -> backend responds with 504 after ~30s, connection closed. Attaching raw tcpdump trace shows repeated SYN/ACK then no application-level response.
liam: timeline check — rollout finished 08:22; errors start 08:34. Possibly slow warmup under load or new kernel parameters. I'm going to check autoscaler events and GPU recycler logs.
liam: checking autoscaler: ``kubectl -n runtime get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=worker-group-eu-1`` -> several "OOMKilled" and "backoff" events at 08:33 for worker-x93.
liam: looks like a memory pressure/eviction pattern; workers restart then take time to warm KV cache, causing higher latency and proxy timeouts during warmup window.
natalie: suggested mitigations — 1) revert canary -> roll back to runtime-release/2026.03.14 on cluster-eu-1 (if confirmed), 2) temporarily increase proxy upstream timeout to 45s as safety, 3) enable model fallback to smaller replica for affected tenants. Which do we want first?
liam: immediate: increase proxy timeout to 45s for /v1/generate route on eu-ingress (low risk, quick). Also adjust alerting: lower noise by adding dimension on upstream_host so we alert on host-level cascading failures, not transient single-host restarts.
